key_insight: Pangram 4 is a highly accurate AI-text detector that improves on Pangram 3, achieving very strong classification performance while better handling out-of-distribution text and adversarial attempts to evade detection. It also appears more capable of spotting fine-grained edits and mixed AI-human content.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of reliably distinguishing AI-generated text from human-written text, especially when the content is edited, mixed, or intentionally crafted to bypass detection systems.
method: Developed Pangram 4, a deep-learning-based AI-text classification model.
Evaluated the model using standard detection metrics, including AUROC, false positive rate, and false negative rate.
Tested robustness on out-of-distribution examples and adversarially manipulated text to assess real-world reliability.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work offers a stronger and more robust detection system for identifying synthetic text in practical settings. Its improved resilience to distribution shifts and adversarial edits makes it especially relevant for content moderation, provenance checks, and trust-and-safety workflows.
visual_elements: Performance dashboard with AUROC, false positive rate, and false negative rate highlighted

paper_authors: Ben Glickenhaus, Katherine Thai, Jenna Russell, Elyas Masrour, Yue Han
